concept.title: Still Learning Love
concept.human_truth: Healthy love is not proved by never contradicting yourself; it is proved by noticing the pattern sooner and repairing with more softness than last time.
concept.reference_theme: I talk about a value, but I still fail at it sometimes.
concept.a_story_translation: We talk about healthy love, but we are still learning it in real time through tone, listening, space, apologies, and repair.
concept.format: 7-slide Instagram carousel, native 1080x1440 post handoff with separate 1080x1920 reels/stories handoff when generated

slides.copy:
we talk about healthy love,
but we still learn it mid-fight.
slides.visual: Immediate cover contradiction: Aachu and Zuv are mid-fight in a lived-in room, verbally tense but not cruel. Their bodies are angled away, hands animated, brows tight, with tiny signs they still care: one cup between them, a blanket half-shared, feet still pointed toward each other. Make it active, not quiet poster sadness.
slides.emotion: active conflict, honest, still loving underneath
slides.story_director_job: Stop the scroll with the honest contradiction and make the fight theme immediately legible.

slides.copy:
we talk about patience,
but sometimes our tone arrives first.
slides.visual: Show the two verbally fighting or sharply talking over each other in a kitchen or small room. One partner points or lifts a hand mid-sentence while the other reacts, a cup/spoon/object landing too hard on the counter. The receipt is tone arriving before patience: visible mouths open, tense hands, not physical aggression.
slides.emotion: sharp tone, verbal fight, not cruel
slides.story_director_job: Stage the first specific verbal-fight behavior that proves the contradiction.

slides.copy:
we talk about listening,
but sometimes we just don't listen at all.
slides.visual: Stage a clear not-listening beat: both partners are in the same room but mentally elsewhere, one talking while the other looks away at a phone, cupboard, or floor; or both speak at once with crossed eye-lines. It should feel instantly recognizable: they are hearing sound, not receiving each other.
slides.emotion: recognizable frustration, talked past each other
slides.story_director_job: Make viewers recognize how not-listening looks inside a relationship.

slides.copy:
we talk about giving space,
but still always irritate the hell out of each other.
slides.visual: Action over words: one partner tries to get space on a bed, sofa, or floor corner, while the other keeps hovering nearby and irritating them in a petty familiar way: poking, making faces, moving a pillow, tapping the door, or standing too close. Make it funny-irritating, not mean.
slides.story_director_job: Carry the truth through familiar irritation and failed space.

slides.copy:
we talk about saying sorry,
but never apologies when we should.
slides.visual: Show the apology failure actively: both partners are close enough to repair but stubbornly not apologizing. One holds a cup or folded arms; the other looks away with a wounded-but-proud face. The apology is available in the room but withheld. No peaceful tea apology; this beat is the stubborn silence after the fight.
slides.story_director_job: Repeat the contradiction through the stubborn apology gap.

slides.copy:
we talk about forever,
but we fight like we don't know each other.
slides.visual: The strongest fight receipt: late evening, both tired and emotional, standing/sitting apart like strangers in their own room. Their posture says they know each other deeply, but the fight has made them act unfamiliar. Use distance, crossed eye-lines, scattered blanket/cups, and one small shared object between them.
slides.emotion: painful turn, stranger-like fight, still intimate underneath
slides.story_director_job: Sharpen the reversal: forever-talk versus stranger-like fighting.

slides.copy:
maybe love is noticing the pattern,
and choosing softness sooner.
slides.visual: Morning-after or after-fight payoff: the fight energy softens through action, not a grand hug. One partner reaches first, adjusts a blanket, moves closer, or offers a small touch; the other accepts. The room still has traces of the fight, but the body language shows they noticed the pattern sooner.
slides.story_director_job: Land the saveable lesson through a visible choice toward softness.

caption_options:
we are not perfect at the love we believe in.

some days patience comes late.
sorry comes as a cup.
forever becomes one repaired evening.

maybe the point is not never repeating the pattern.
maybe it is noticing sooner,
and coming back softer.
for the couples who are still learning the love they keep choosing.
copy.posting_notes: Keep the caption quiet. Do not mention the reference account publicly. If posted, the carousel itself carries the theme.

visual_setup: Action-forward fight/repair carousel: the couple verbally fights, fails to listen, irritates each other, withholds apologies, then notices the pattern and chooses softness sooner.
